title: I Helped My Friend Launch Her Bakery in One Weekend
creator: Lucia Ferrante
description:
My best friend Rosa has been baking out of her apartment for two years. This weekend we gave her a menu, photos and a real website.

Rosa's pastry Instagram: @rosabakes

Camera: borrowed. Croissants: eaten.

sentences.t: This is Rosa, she is my best friend, and she makes the best croissants I have ever eaten, and I've been to Paris.
For two years she's been selling them out of her apartment through text messages and a very chaotic spreadsheet.
This weekend we're fixing that.
By Sunday night, she's going to have a real menu, real photos, and a real website where people can order.
Rosa, how do you feel?
She says terrified, which is fair.
Okay, Saturday morning, step one is the menu.
Rosa makes something like fifteen different things, and the problem is that nobody knows what to order.
So we sat down with coffee and cut it to six, the three things people order the most and three seasonal ones.
The croissants stay, obviously, the cardamom buns stay, and the sourdough loaf stays.
The seasonal ones this month are a pear tart, a pumpkin cinnamon roll, and a chocolate rye cookie that I would personally go to war for.
Step two, photos.
We set up a little table by her window with a linen cloth, because natural light makes pastry look incredible and harsh kitchen lights make it look sad.
The trick is to shoot from slightly above, and get one shot where something is broken open, so you can see the layers inside.
I ate a lot of props this weekend, and I regret nothing.
Okay, it's Saturday afternoon and it's time to build the actual website, and Pagecraft sponsored this part of the video, so thanks to them for that.
I'm opening Pagecraft and picking a blank template, because Rosa's vibe is not the stock bakery look with chalkboards everywhere.
First I'm setting her colors, a warm cream for the background and that deep terracotta from her apron for the buttons.
Now I'm dragging in a big header block and dropping in the photo of the croissant broken open, with her name over it in a simple serif font.
Under that, I'm adding a menu section, and I'm uploading each of the six photos with the name, price, and one short line about it.
Rosa wrote the descriptions herself, and the one for the cookie just says trust me, which I think is perfect.
Next is ordering, so I'm turning on the order form, setting pickup on Fridays and Saturdays only, and limiting it to forty orders a day so she doesn't burn out.
Then I'm connecting her domain, which we bought for about twelve dollars, and checking the mobile preview, because almost everyone is going to order from their phone.
And there it is, live.
Rosa just made a noise I've never heard a human make.
Sunday, launch day.
She posted the link on her Instagram at nine in the morning, and we sat on the couch refreshing the orders page like it was an election night.
The first order came in at nine oh four, from her cousin, which we're counting.
By noon she had twenty-three orders, and by the evening, she had sold out of croissants for the whole next week.
I think the biggest change isn't even the website, it's that she finally sees this as a real business and not a hobby that got out of hand.
She's already talking about renting a commercial kitchen in the spring.
If you're in the area, go order a cookie, and tell her I sent you.
Thank you for watching, and I'll see you next week.
